title: A calm triage method
subtitle: Gather evidence, narrow the blast radius, change one thing at a time.
objectives: Apply a repeatable triage method under pressure
Run a first-pass health check in the right order
Match common symptoms to the most useful evidence
Avoid random changes that destroy the evidence trail
Write a clear escalation with timeline and impact

sections.title: The method beats the memorized command
Escalate with a timeline, not a vibe

commands.desc: List units that failed to start.
Show error-priority messages from this boot.
Check inode exhaustion on the root filesystem.
Show a compact interface and address summary.
List listening sockets and owning processes.
Trace permissions on every path component.

lab.title: Run a calm first pass
lab.scenario: Perform a non-destructive health assessment and write a three-line situation report from the evidence.

steps.text: Capture system identity, uptime, and load.
steps.verify: The output should identify the host, its uptime, and the current load averages.

steps.text: List failed units and recent error-priority journal entries.
steps.verify: The failed-unit list should be empty or explain the failure; the journal should show recent errors.
No filesystem should be near 100 percent; note inode use and available memory.

steps.text: Check addresses, routes, and listening sockets.
steps.cmd: ip -br addr; ip route; sudo ss -tulpn
steps.verify: Confirm the interface, the default route, and the listening ports.

steps.text: Review the last package transactions for recent change.
steps.verify: dnf history should show the most recent transactions and their dates.

steps.text: Write a three-line report: impact, evidence, next action. Keep it factual and time-stamped.
steps.verify: If nothing is wrong, say so and include the evidence you checked.

quiz.q: A service is failing. What should you capture before restarting it?
options: A new screenshot of the desktop
quiz.why: Restarting can clear the state that explains the failure. Capture status and logs first when safe.

quiz.q: df shows free blocks but writes fail. What is the next check?
quiz.why: A filesystem can run out of inodes while blocks remain free. df -i confirms it.

quiz.q: Why change only one thing at a time during triage?
options: It preserves causality and prevents new problems
quiz.why: Multiple simultaneous changes make it impossible to know what worked or what broke.
